Question: A binary operation \(\diamondsuit\) has the properties that \[a\,\diamondsuit\, (b\,\diamondsuit \,c) = (a\,\diamondsuit \,b)\cdot c\] and that \(a\,\diamondsuit \,a=1\) for all nonzero real numbers \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c.\) (Here the dot \(\cdot\) represents the usual multiplication operation.) The solution to the equation \[2016 \,\diamondsuit\, (6\,\diamondsuit\, x)=100\] can be written as \(\frac{p}{q},\) where \(p\) and \(q\) are relatively prime positive integers. What is \(p+q?\)
